findings.claim: "The Scrum Master serves the organization in several ways, including: Leading, training, and coaching ... and, Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams."
findings.evidence: Deep ref L94 [V]; matches source L354-365.

findings.claim: customers/users (implicit in "value", "the Increment must be usable" [V])
findings.failure_mode: understates the source: users and customers are named explicitly
findings.evidence: Deep ref L187 [V]: 'A product is a vehicle to deliver value. It has a clear boundary, known stakeholders, well-defined users or customers.' (Scrum Artifacts, 'Product Backlog', 'Commitment: Product Goal').
findings.fix: correct: customers/users (named in the Guide's definition of a product: "known stakeholders, well-defined users or customers" [V])

findings.claim: "The Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. ..." [V]
findings.evidence: Deep ref L157 and source L506: 'The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.' The distillation drops 'purpose of the'.
findings.fix: correct: "The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done." [V]

findings.claim: the Scrum Team (coaching, focus on Increments, impediment removal, event facilitation)
findings.failure_mode: accountability paraphrased into a different one
findings.evidence: Deep ref L92: 'Ensuring that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox'. The Guide does not make the Scrum Master the facilitator of the events; 'Facilitating' appears only for stakeholder collaboration (L93).
findings.fix: correct: the Scrum Team (coaching, focus on Increments, impediment removal, ensuring events take place and stay productive and within the timebox)

findings.claim: The Sprint Review is "to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations" [V]: not a status report, not a demo, not a sign-off ceremony.
findings.evidence: Deep ref L149, L151: 'The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders'; the team 'should avoid limiting it to a presentation'. Presenting results is part of the event; the Guide rules out limiting it to that, not showing work.
findings.fix: correct: ... not a status report, not only a demo, not a sign-off ceremony.

findings.claim: "The rest of the Product Backlog emerges to define 'what' will fulfill the Product Goal."
findings.evidence: Deep ref L183 [V]; matches source L562-563.

findings.claim: "The rest of the Product Backlog emerges to define 'what' will fulfill the Product Goal"
the Product Owner moves the UX-redesign item from Sprint 7 to Sprint 5 in the room
findings.failure_mode: example assigns items to future Sprints, which the Guide does not do
findings.evidence: Deep ref L74: the PO orders Product Backlog items. L127: at Sprint Planning 'the Developers select items from the Product Backlog to include in the current Sprint'. Items are not pre-assigned to numbered Sprints.
findings.fix: correct: the Product Owner moves the UX-redesign item near the top of the Product Backlog in the room

findings.claim: The Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience model provides the stakeholder-mapping theory the Scrum Guide lacks.
findings.failure_mode: concept attributed to the wrong corpus source
findings.evidence: openstax-business-ethics-deep.md Part III (L101-126) carries Donaldson-Preston, Grunig-Hunt categories and a power x interest matrix with exigency (Ch 3.3); Mitchell-Agle-Wood does not appear in that deep ref or its converted source. It appears in jones-evidence-based-sweng-deep.md (Ch 5.4.5).
findings.fix: correct: Business Ethics' stakeholder prioritisation (power x interest matrix, with exigency raising priority; Ch 3.3) and Grunig-Hunt stakeholder categories provide the stakeholder-mapping theory the Scrum Guide lacks.

findings.claim: Provides the broad theory of group dynamics, communication networks, leadership, power, conflict, and negotiation
findings.failure_mode: content attributed to the other source that its deep ref does not carry
findings.evidence: openstax-organizational-behavior-deep.md Part XI (L330-350) covers the communication model and feedback types; communication networks appear in neither the deep ref nor the converted source.
findings.fix: correct: group dynamics, communication, leadership, power, conflict, and negotiation

findings.claim: The Scrum Master as a "true leader who serves" maps to OB's servant-leadership literature
findings.failure_mode: concept attributed to the wrong corpus source
findings.evidence: No 'servant' passage in openstax-organizational-behavior-deep.md. Greenleaf servant leadership is in openstax-principles-management-deep.md L247 (anchors Ch 5.4, L979).
findings.fix: correct: strip from the OB row; the servant-leadership link belongs to the Principles of Management row (Ch 5.4).

findings.claim: 1-2-4-All inside Sprint Planning's "Why is this Sprint valuable?" [V] topic
findings.failure_mode: structure named by the wider LS canon, not this handbook
findings.evidence: liberating-structures-handbook-deep.md L59, L194: the handbook names it '1-2-4-Whole Group'. '1-2-4-All' does not occur in that deep ref or its source. What/So What/Now What (After Action Debrief, L113), Wise Crowds (L77) and Knee-to-Knee Conversation (L53) hold.

findings.claim: servant leadership theory is the OB frame nearest the Guide's "true leaders who serve" [V] framing
findings.evidence: Servant leadership (Greenleaf) is carried by openstax-principles-management-deep.md L247 (Ch 5.4), not by Organizational Behavior.
findings.fix: correct: Principles of Management's Greenleaf servant leadership (Ch 5.4) is the frame nearest the Guide's "true leaders who serve" [V] framing

findings.claim: Scrum's role-based engagement structures are the explicit design Open Kanban deliberately avoids.
findings.failure_mode: other source's position overstated into an explicit contrast
findings.evidence: open-kanban-deep.md L152: 'Although Kanban starts where you are, and does not need to modify any titles or roles in an organization, Kanban cannot work without a team to deliver value' [V]. Open Kanban does not position itself against Scrum's roles.
findings.fix: correct: Open Kanban "does not need to modify any titles or roles in an organization" but "cannot work without a team to deliver value" [V]; Scrum instead defines three accountabilities.

findings.fix: correct: uses only [V] markers (125 [V] across 102 lines; no [BT], [AP], [AR], or [AE] markers)

notes: All other [V] quotations checked against sources/converted/scrum-guide-2020.md and are exact or clean substrings. Timeboxes (4 h, 3 h, 15 min) and the Scrum Master's three principals check. Integration rows that hold: Letaw (Tuckman, fist of five, requirements elicitation, paper prototyping with think-aloud, Inclusivity Heuristics), OPL (Showcase/Sprint Review, $100, MoSCoW, RICE, Dot Voting, Stakeholders Interview, Empathy Mapping), Principles of Management Mintzberg roles. The Business Ethics row repeats the Mitchell-Agle-Wood misattribution found in the decision-making and software-business distillations.
